beats.objective: Take soup to {friend.first} before the night shift
Decide whose door you reach first
Bring the last ration box to {keeper.first}
Bring the last ration box to {friend.first}
Deliver the tin to the Lamplighter
Decide what the key is for
Take the key to the sealed door

first_night.speaker: patron
first_night.text: {patron.first} {patron.family} slides a warm bag across the counter of {patron.place}. "[Rent's due Monday, courier|You look like you need the work]. Orders come in every hour. Find the door, keep it hot, don't feed the gangs."

keeper_door.speaker: keeper
keeper_door.text: The door opens a crack. {keeper.first} {keeper.family}, old and sharp-eyed, counts the coins twice. "You're new. The last one never came this deep." On the shelf behind them sits a dented tin, polished like a relic.

friend_door.speaker: friend
friend_door.text: {friend.first} {friend.family} takes the soup with both hands. "[Twelve hours on the ward|Another double shift] and you're the first face that didn't want something from me. Come by again, will you?"

rival.speaker: rival
rival.text: A courier in a patched jacket cuts in front of you at the counter and grabs your next order. "{rival.first}. Remember it — this stretch was mine before you showed up."

blight.speaker: patron
blight.text: {patron.first} pins a new price list over the old one. "The blight's in the farm layers. {monopolist.name} says supply is short, so everything costs three times as much. Funny how their warehouses never run dry."

rationing.speaker: patron
rationing.text: "One ration box left tonight," {patron.first} says. "{keeper.first} hasn't eaten since yesterday. {friend.first}'s ward lost its kitchen. Your call, courier."

ration_keeper.speaker: keeper
ration_keeper.text: {keeper.first} holds the box like it might vanish. "My great-aunt used to say the city was built on a lie about how little there is." The tin is on the table now.

ration_friend.speaker: friend
ration_friend.text: {friend.first} shares the box out among the night staff before taking a bite. "Someone's sitting on food while people faint in the corridors. I'll remember who brought this."

hijack.speaker: disruptor
hijack.text: Word runs down the corridors: {disruptor.name} hijacked two couriers on the bridges last night and sold the food at blight prices. They know your face now.

rally.speaker: idealists
rally.text: In the stairwell, people from {idealists.name} press leaflets into every hand: OPEN THE WAREHOUSES. "Couriers go everywhere," one says. "Carry a few for us?"

keeper_call.speaker: keeper
keeper_call.text: A message on the courier board, in shaky capitals: COME TOMORROW. THERE IS SOMETHING I MUST GIVE YOU BEFORE THEY DO. — {keeper.first} {keeper.family}

keeper_dies.speaker: patron
keeper_dies.text: {patron.first} meets you at the counter without a bag. "{keeper.first} {keeper.family} died in the night. They left an order on the board, paid in full: a sealed tin, for 'the Lamplighter'. The address has been a burnt-out flat since the Blackout."

lamplighter_door.speaker: lamplighter
lamplighter_door.text: The door of {lamplighter.name}'s flat hangs open on soot and silence. Nobody has lived here for a century. Inside the tin: an old doorway key and a journal signed by the Lamplighter herself — a map to a founders' vault of living seed. By morning, the whole corridor seems to know you have it.

everyone_knows.speaker: monopolist
everyone_knows.text: A courier from {monopolist.name} leaves a card at {patron.place}: NAME YOUR PRICE. {disruptor.name} send a simpler message: a cracked bowl on your doorstep. {patron.first} watches you read both.

medicine_door.speaker: friend
medicine_door.text: {friend.first} takes the tonic with shaking hands. "Half the ward has the blight cough now. {monopolist.name} sells this at ten times cost." They squeeze your arm. "Be careful. People are asking about you."

testimony_door.speaker: organizer
testimony_door.text: {organizer.first} {organizer.family} of {idealists.name} plugs in the drive and goes pale. "Shipping logs. {monopolist.name} moved the blight spores into the farm layers themselves. With this and that seed vault, we could open the warehouses for good."

friend_hurt.speaker: disruptor
friend_hurt.text: You find {friend.first} on the ward's own bed, bruised and furious. {disruptor.name} came asking where the courier keeps the key. "I didn't tell them," {friend.first} says. "Go. Before they ask someone weaker."

vault.speaker: vault
vault.text: Behind {vault.name}, deep under the district, the key turns. Cold air, green light: rack after rack of living seed, enough to feed the Reach for a generation. Footsteps on the stairs behind you. Who gets it?

choices.text: Give it to {disruptor.name} for their protection.
Lock it again and lose the key.

epilogue_public.speaker: idealists
epilogue_public.text: Within a week the seed is in every farm layer. Food prices fall for the first time in living memory. {organizer.first} names the new co-op after {keeper.first} {keeper.family}.

epilogue_monopolist.speaker: monopolist
epilogue_monopolist.text: {monopolist.name} pays well — very well. The vault is emptied by morning, and prices stay where they were. {friend.first} stops answering your knocks.

epilogue_disruptor.speaker: disruptor
epilogue_disruptor.text: {disruptor.name} hand out seed like favours and take every bridge in the district as their price. Nobody hijacks your deliveries any more. Nobody crosses without paying, either.

epilogue_hidden.speaker: keeper
epilogue_hidden.text: The key goes into the fog off a high bridge. Somewhere below, the founders' vault sleeps again. Maybe the next Lamplighter will choose better. Maybe there is no better choice.
